plugins.audit_text:
[`aae_plugin.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-plugin-aae/src/lib/aae_plugin.rs):937–1070 mixes direct stereo, early reflections, allpass diffusion and an FDN late field into surround channels, with dialogue ducking and smoothed gains. Its recursive state makes silence-start, reset and tail policy central. Equal-power predelay crossfades can boost highly correlated taps; measure the transition peak rather than assuming constant amplitude. FDN work scales with output configuration and delay network complexity.

`autogain_clock.rs`, `autogain_heap.rs` and integration tests exercise important control/RT behavior. Extend measured decay-time and frequency-dependent damping checks, echo density, channel decorrelation and worst-case predelay changes. Classical improvements: controlled early-reflection geometry, frequency-dependent RT60 and correlation-aware crossfades. ML is most sensible as offline fitting of these parameters to a measured room; retain a bounded deterministic renderer.

tasks.requirement: Remove coherent predelay crossfade boost without changing latency.
tasks.result: Public regression failed at 44.1 kHz with maximum wet-signal difference 0.0007968461 (wet peak 0.0075587574). A constant-sum smoothstep crossfade passes at 44.1/48/96 kHz; full crate selection passed 95 tests.

tasks.requirement: Eliminate correlated delay-transition amplification inside late-network feedback.
tasks.result: Near-identical room-size update reproduced 1.04834384e-4 waveform error at 44.1 kHz despite unchanged integer delays. Constant-sum smoothstep replaces equal-power weights in both static and modulated FDN read heads; all 12 rate/modulation cases match the unchanged twin exactly. Fixed 10 ms duration, parameter/schema/latency/storage contracts unchanged. Eight interrupted extreme-room cases assert finite output, completed transition and zero allocations/frees.

tasks.requirement: Measure isolated neutral RT60, treble damping and existing renderer echo density/spatial behavior.
tasks.result: 18 stationary low-level summed-tap-energy T30 cases span 44.1/48/96 kHz, room sizes 0.2/1/3 and neutral RT60 0.5/2 seconds. Maximum target error 0.5805%, minimum r2 0.9919648, under 10% and above 0.98 bounds. Longer T30 fit was selected after sparse-room T20 quality limitation; both observations retained. Three high-band T20 damping checks shorten neutral ~1.204 s to ~0.837 s. Existing four-preset quality runner passes with normalized echo density 1.254-1.300, mixing times 0.267-0.298 s, spatial coherence 0.1445-0.5802. Preset matrix shares default late controls; no arbitrary preset RT60 claim.

tasks.requirement: Eliminate discontinuous nonlinear feedback at the safety threshold and validate recursive sensitivity.
tasks.result: Feedback soft_clip previously used identity through the ceiling then ceiling*tanh(x/ceiling), producing a -0.23839164 normalized jump at threshold. Threshold-adjacent impulses reproduced 0.22968596 peak recursive sample difference. Continuous odd monotone C1 half-ceiling knee now preserves small-signal unity and remains bounded by the same configured ceiling. 131076 signed grid probes at four ceilings assert bounds, monotonicity, symmetry and low-level identity; knee slopes match unity. 24 three-second recursive renders span 44.1/48/96/192 kHz, room 0.2/3 and modulation 0/0.5/1; worst difference 8.165836e-06, no allocations. Full release 102 passed, strict all-target QA Clippy and offline quality diagnostic pass; only printed quality change is high-level limiter_activity final_gain 0.322765 -> 0.322770; all other acoustic/detector rows unchanged. Existing neutral T30/treble damping and interrupted room-change heap tests pass. High-level feedback tails intentionally change above half ceiling; delay, latency, parameters, presets and storage unchanged. No universal nonlinear RT60, finite-tail, listening or device-deadline claim.

tasks.requirement: Preserve noncorrelated active room fades under interruption, coalesce bounded targets and reset to the requested endpoint.
tasks.result: Interrupted noncorrelated room fades reproduced 0.0037842088 sample deviation from the uninterrupted active fade. One fixed latest-target slot now preserves both active heads until their 10ms fade finishes, then admits a new 10ms fade. Superseded targets coalesce; requesting the active endpoint cancels pending work without restarting the fade. Damping gains are prepared in setters, refreshed on independent RT60/bass/treble edits, and applied on admission without power calculations, allocation or extra read heads. Reset installs requested room/decay and clears coefficient ramps plus recursive state. 24 four-rate/two-modulation/three-interruption cases are sample-exact against two staged complete fades; eight each validate cancellation, independent decay admission and reset-to-fresh endpoint. Eight admission/reset cases and existing interrupted-room tests have zero allocations/frees. Full release 107 tests pass, strict all-target QA Clippy/format pass; printed acoustic-quality output is byte-identical to prior. Fixed signal latency, serialized settings and delay buffer capacity unchanged. After requests stop, latest room completes within remaining active fade plus one fade; no perceptual or native-deadline claim.

tasks.requirement: Preserve noncorrelated predelay fade ownership through worst-range interrupted updates and endpoint lifecycle.
tasks.result: Public noncorrelated predelay retargeting reproduced 0.0012540973 output error versus two uninterrupted fades. One latest pending target now preserves the active 10ms fade before starting the queued 10ms fade; supersession coalesces and active-destination requests cancel pending work. Reset/initialize install requested delay and clear pending state, including zero. 24 exact public-plugin staged-twin cases span four rates, three interruption phases, 50/100ms destinations (maximum supported 100ms), zero-delay final target and 31/257-frame partitions. Eight reset/reinitialization fresh-twin and four cancellation cases are exact; four prepared setter/admission/reset heap cases allocate/free nothing. Full release 111 passed before extending the existing test to 100ms; final expanded focused suite three passed and strict all-target QA Clippy/format pass. Offline acoustic-quality printed output unchanged. No schema/preset/direct latency/delay buffer change; latest requested delay settles within remaining active fade plus one 10ms fade after requests stop. No listening or native-deadline claim.

plugins.audit_text:
[`abcompare_plugin.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-plugin-ab-compare/src/lib/abcompare_plugin.rs):2200–2400 handles nested processing paths, differing rate/frame geometry, latency alignment and queued finite tails. This is a transport/composition component as much as an effect. Two expensive chains plus alignment buffering create significant worst-case cost. A fair comparison requires equal source time, aligned latency and a stable loudness-matching policy.

`aud137_composition.rs`, `aud137_finite_stream.rs`, `ab087_variable_rate.rs` and `loudness_timing.rs` provide unusually relevant coverage. Add blinded ABX selection, frozen gain matching during judged excerpts, switch-click measurements and source-change tests during partial queued output. Use classical equal-loudness/time-alignment tools; ML should not decide which sound is “better” or secretly modify either comparison path.

Both assignments exercised deterministically and public reveal checked at 44.1/48/96 kHz.

plugins.audit_text:
[`aec_plugin.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-plugin-aec/src/lib/aec_plugin.rs):312–490 adapts a microphone/reference pair to mono output with block buffering, resettable adaptive/postfilter state and finite draining that freezes learning. It consumes pending output before accumulating the next block, which helps block partition consistency. Reference alignment and the first adaptation interval matter more than a steady-state cancellation number.

`stream_boundaries.rs` and integration tests cover stream mechanics. Extend independent echo-path ground truth with delay jumps, clock drift, nonlinear loudspeaker distortion, near-end-only speech and double-talk. Report ERLE only during suitable far-end intervals, plus near-end speech distortion. Classical options include robust delay estimation, two-path adaptation and coherence-based double-talk control. A small neural residual-echo suppressor/nonlinear front end is a credible hybrid candidate [hybrid AEC research][R3]; keep adaptive cancellation and safe bypass operational without inference.

tasks.requirement: Track in-tail delay changes and fractional clock drift without starving background adaptation.
tasks.result: Background learning stays active. Foreground promotion requires squared correlation >=0.5 and >=1 dB smoothed improvement for 133 ms initially, 25 ms thereafter. Delay-jump ERLE improves from 1.8–2.9 dB to 28.0–35.6 dB without the post-filter. Both signs of 100 ppm drift reach 4.4–9.6 dB without suppression, 13.9–17.2 dB with it. The documented regression floor is 3 dB; there is no clock synchronization.

tasks.requirement: Preserve independent near-end audio, including quiet onsets, double-talk and near-end-only audio after learned echo.
tasks.result: Residual coherence and a rise above the learned floor prevent quiet near-end assimilation into leakage. Three near-end levels (0.25/1/2) pass >=10 dB SNR, with observed minimum 20.58 dB including onset. Quiet post-filter baseline was 1.29–1.80 dB SNR. Cold/after-echo near-end-only segments exceed 139 dB SNR with the post-filter.

tasks.requirement: Use independent echo-path ground truth, separate far-end ERLE from near-end distortion, and verify reference alignment, initial adaptation and partitions.
tasks.result: 60 scene/rate/post-filter combinations at 16/44.1/48 kHz use independently generated two-tap, fractional-delay and nonlinear echo. Regular and 193/1/511/67 callbacks are bit-identical. The exact 256-frame latency and first output block are checked independently. Eight 250 ms convergence windows per linear case report initial learning; onset and far-end recovery are measured separately.

tasks.requirement: Preserve reset, frozen finite drain, constructor timing, parameters and realtime allocation contracts.
tasks.result: Full release QA-feature selection: 63 tests passed, including frozen nonzero-tail oracles and cold callback/drain/reset allocation checks. Strict all-target QA Clippy passes. No parameter/preset schema change or inference dependency.

validation_limits: Independent deterministic colored-noise engineering fixtures, not recorded speech or perceptual results.
One 50 ms prepared tail and default 0.5 step at three rates; no out-of-tail compensation, clock synchronization or universal ERLE guarantee.
The initial 6 dB drift target is not achieved at 48 kHz without suppression; the final 3 dB regression floor documents half-power reduction.
Neural residual echo/nonlinear models remain deferred optional research in the separate backlog.

plugins.audit_text:
[`ambisonics_decoder_plugin.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-plugin-ambisonics/src/lib/ambisonics_decoder_plugin.rs):376–520 combines decoding matrices with optional LR4 dual-band basic/max-rE behavior. Matrix-only processing is rate independent; dual-band processing is not. The process path validates shape/finite samples but should consistently enforce the initialized sample rate for rate-sensitive modes. Recursive crossover support must not be confused with a finite zero-latency tail.

`decode_vectors.rs`, `custom_layouts.rs`, `aud133_baseline.rs` and `tail_support.rs` are appropriate foundations. Extend analytic ACN/normalization and spherical-harmonic basis checks, rotation covariance, energy/vector errors and ill-conditioned speaker layouts. Classical regularized/layout-aware decoding is preferable to ML replacing the normative decoder. Learned personalization may choose an HRTF/layout correction offline, with explicit normalization and energy constraints.

ACN round trips and SN3D mean-square 1/(2l+1) are checked.

FOA octahedral output energy and Gerzon velocity/energy vectors match independent closed-form laws within 2e-6. AllRAD finite-grid rotation feed error is 0.005737289786338806 and relative energy error 0.0041178252346234226 in the tested FOA geometry, below fixed 0.05 feed/vector and 5% energy bounds; exact continuous covariance is explicitly not claimed for the fixed grid.

plugins.audit_text:
[`delay_plugin.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-plugin-delay/src/lib/delay_plugin.rs):972–1125 resets delay/LFO/crossfade histories and drains bounded nonrecursive support. For feedback/recursive routes, native drain can report complete rather than synthesize an unbounded tail. That may be an intentional host contract, but a renderer must not assume all audible repeats are automatically emitted at EOF.

`audit_accuracy.rs`, `tail_length.rs`, `finite_stream.rs`, property and realtime parameter tests provide good foundations. Add end-to-end offline render tests with an explicit tail-duration/energy policy, feedback near its limit, delay changes and tempo discontinuities. Classical fractional delay, click-free dual taps and tape-style pitch modulation should be separate, tested modes. ML is unnecessary for the basic delay.

host_analyzers_and_adapters.audit_text:
**Spectrum analyzer.** [`analyzer_spectrum.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-host/src/analyzer_spectrum.rs):425–545 enforces initialization/rate, retains a recent-sample ring and computes channel power without cancellation from summing opposite-phase channels. It analyzes the most recent window after a block; a block spanning multiple FFT windows can omit intermediate windows. That is acceptable for a display only if specified, but unsuitable for guaranteed transient/peak capture. Extend calibrated bin-centered/off-bin tones, DC/Nyquist, impulses, channel anti-phase and arbitrary callback sizes. Offer explicit amplitude/PSD normalization and max-hold semantics. No ML is needed for a calibrated spectrum.

**Loudness monitor.** [`analyzer_loudness_monitor.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-host/src/analyzer_loudness_monitor.rs):2029–2089 preserves transparent audio, validates shape/rate and finalizes true-peak state at drain. This is a stronger EOF contract than simply stopping the meter. Extend independent conformance vectors, short clips, gating discontinuities, surround channel weights, disabled/re-enabled state and final publication under cache contention. Distinguish LUFS from psychoacoustic loudness/SPL. ML quality scores may be supplementary, never a substitute for calibrated measurement.

**AutoGain.** [`auto_gain.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-host/src/auto_gain.rs):281–395 uses sample-clocked gain trajectories and a settled fast path. Its integration into each effect must measure the intended pre/post stages and handle silence without runaway gain or level jumps. Existing per-plugin clock/heap tests are a major strength. Extend sparse transients, prolonged silence then signal, AB switching and peak-constrained gain recovery. Classical loudness/peak-constrained matching suffices; no learned gain controller is needed by default.

**External plugin factory route.** The `external`/`external_plugin` entry delegates to native formats and may use isolated workers. It inherits the scheduling, latency, parameter, state and sandbox boundaries discussed above, rather than one fixed DSP algorithm. Test process death, stale sequence, missed deadline, malformed state, latency change, instrument MIDI and output-channel changes against real AU/VST3/CLAP fixtures. Compare native and isolated audio after declared pipeline latency; fallback audio must remain distinguishable from successfully processed output. ML is not a substitute for process containment or ABI validation.

**Adapters/support crates.** `plugins-bridge`, `plugins-ffi`, `plugins-nih`, `plugins-gpui`, `plugins-spatial`, `plugins-denoiser` and `plugins-inference` are not seven more standalone DSP effects. They carry ABI, native-host, UI, spatial-data and inference contracts. A plugin passing its own crate tests does not prove its AU/VST3/CLAP/FFI form has correct parameter units, sample offsets, channel negotiation, latency change notification or tail handling. Add cross-wrapper audio equivalence and lifecycle suites, and run native-feature builds on their supported platforms. Inference already uses generation-tagged bounded handoff; retain that architecture and explicitly constrain allocation/destruction and model shutdown.
